images.caption: Figure 1:Architecture of a System 1 agent.a, Components and data flow. The agent asks the decision model typed questions for tool selection, tool fit and the capability check, and passes the chosen tool and the request to the compiler. The compiler turns the tool’s schema into argument questions for the same model and returns the arguments and any missing required values. The agent then prompts the user for a missing required value with a fixed template (the argument’s name and schema description) or sends the MCP call. No step generates text.b, One imaging development request with the decisions recorded from pplx-decider-flash: the tool question over 43 options, the capability check, the compiler’s questions with the options offered and the model’s answers, and the resulting call.

Figure 2:Accuracy of every agent.a, Tool calling: the right tool for a complete request or a decline for an out-of-scope request (n = 1,952 requests).b, Argument filling: stated values right in a call to the right tool (n = 6,056 values).c, Fully correct requests: for a complete request, the labelled tool with every stated value right and no required argument left empty; for an out-of-scope request, a decline (n = 1,952). Points show proportions; error bars show 95% Wilson intervals (a,c) and 95% bootstrap intervals over requests (b). Agents are ordered by fully correct requests; System 1 agents are in bold.

Figure 3:Pairwise comparison of System 1 and LLM agents.Difference in percentage points (System 1 agent minus LLM-based agent) for each System 1 agent (columns) and each LLM-based agent in each reasoning mode (rows), fora, fully correct requests,b, tool calling andc, argument filling. Shaded cells are significant after Holm correction over the 108 pairs of each measure (adjusted P < 0.05; exact McNemar test ina,b, exact paired sign-flip test inc); outlined cells are not significant. Colours are clipped at ±15 points. Above each panel: pairs with System 1 ahead, LLM ahead and no significant difference.

Figure 4:Reliability evaluation.a, Calls with at least one invented argument value, per agent. Bars show the lower bound and whiskers the upper bound after correcting the automatic check by the precision measured in an independent review (n = 200 flagged values). System 1 agents had none in 10,888 calls.b, Outcomes on the 174 underspecified requests. The correct behaviour is the right tool with the missing required value left for the user; for System 1 agents, every filled value was written elsewhere in the request.c, Out-of-scope requests declined, by kind: far (n = 92), near (n = 153) and modality (n = 62). Points are agents; bars mark the mean of each kind of agent.

Figure 5:Efficiency evaluation.a, Fully correct requests against GPU energy per fully correct request (log scale). Marker shape and colour give the kind of agent and, for LLM agents, the reasoning mode; every agent is labelled. Extended Data Table 6 gives the values.b, Mean time per request, all agents ranked (log scale).
